about: The one place in the Roman Mass that names the sacrifices of the Old Testament: Abel, Abraham and Melchisedech. The same three stand at one altar in the mosaic of Sant'Apollinare in Classe outside Ravenna. The prayer asks God to accept this sacrifice as he accepted theirs — and asks it after the consecration, which gave the medieval commentators trouble. Abel is here púer tuus justus, thy just servant; Melchisedech is summus sacérdos, thy high priest.

s01.narrative: The priest goes on with his hands spread.

s02.translation: Upon these deign to look with a gracious and serene countenance, and to accept them, as thou didst deign to accept the gifts of thy just servant Abel, and the sacrifice of Abraham our patriarch:

s03.translation: and that which thy high priest Melchisedech offered to thee, a holy sacrifice, an unspotted victim.

w002.function: A relative with no antecedent clause, reaching back to the offerings of the prayer before; Latin opens a paragraph this way, English cannot.

w003.function: A word from Roman sacrifice: a propítium god is one whose offering has been received.

w005.function: First said of a cloudless sky, and only then of a face.

w011.function: Accépta habére as in the Te ígitur: to hold as received, to enter on the list of the accepted.

w015.function: A deponent participle with es: passive in form, active in meaning, and perfect in tense.

w016.function: The auxiliary: the tense is carried by the participle “dignátus” (w015), which is what the gloss renders.

w018.function: Puer means both boy and servant, as Greek país does.

w021.function: An indeclinable name: only “púeri” (w018), which it stands in apposition to, shows the genitive.

w026.function: The one of the three names Latin declines: Ábraham, Ábrahæ.

w028.function: A relative with no antecedent: that which he offered. Two appositions close the sentence after it.

w031.function: The superlative of súperus, upper; this adjective has no positive degree.

w034.function: Indeclinable: the nominative follows from its apposition to “sacérdos” (w032). Hebrews makes him the figure of Christ's priesthood.

w036.function: In apposition to “quod” (w028): the thing he offered — a holy sacrifice.
